chapter: Big bands, small groups and studio work
title: Teddy Wilson

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Let's talk about Teddy Wilson a little bit.

Oh Teddy, Teddy is just great. See I'll never forget when Teddy first came to New York is when I was first with Benny Carter. Benny sent for him, Teddy Wislon, and Keg Johnson, is where they joined. And I thought then, I used to love Earl Hines piano playing, but Teddy was just a step ahead of him I thought as far as swinging was concerned, and I still think that Teddy, boy, is one of the greatest swing pianist there is in techniq and everything else. I just love his playing. So easy to play with.
Do you play a lot of brushes when you play with him?

Yeah, and then sometimes you can play sticks with Teddy, but I always, when I played with Teddy, all according to how large the group is, if it's a trio you play a lot of brushes with Teddy and he's got a lot of piano, things that he's doing, play a lot of brushes.
I heard him a couple of years ago with a trio and doing 'After You've Gone', like way up. No problem. Sounds great.
Oh yeah. Oh boy, wonderful. Easy to listen to. Beautiful.
